Given the strategic role of public procurement in the new Political Guidelines for 2024-2029, the European Commission recognises its significant contribution to a resilient, sustainable and innovative European economy. With more than 250,000 public authorities across Europe spending around €2.3 trillion per year, public procurement stimulates growth, job creation and better public services in key areas such as energy, transport, waste management, health and education.To further unlock this potential, the Commission is continuing its review of the Public Procurement Directive. The reform aims to prioritise European products in strategic sectors and ensure the security of supply of essential technologies, goods and services. It will also modernise and streamline public procurement rules, making them more accessible, in particular for start-ups, innovators and local and regional authorities, while strengthening quality requirements and clarifying the interaction of public procurement rules in different EU legislation. The Public Buyers Community is an initiative supported by DG GROW to strengthen collaboration in the field of public procurement. Contracting authorities can obtain better prices and higher quality goods and services by purchasing together rather than individually. Public buyers can also benefit greatly from the exchange of knowledge and good practices across the EU. European Commission's Directorate for the Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship & SMEs (DG GROW) developed a Public Buyers Platform. This Platform is conceived as a multi-level digital structure combining public and members-only private spaces, to facilitate the exchange of knowledge on public procurement while fostering a safe and confidential environment. It offers subscribers access to the resources that are essential in shaping the future-forward landscape of public procurement in the EEA. The Platform is developed with the aim to enhance cooperation in public procurement - contracting authorities can obtain better prices as well as higher-quality goods and services by buying together instead of individually. Public buyers can also benefit greatly from the exchange of knowledge and best practices across the EU.

title-proc.eng: 10004007_1-Provision of Technical Expert Support on Climate Change Adaptation and Climate Finance in Central and West Africa

description-proc.eng: The regional project "Implementing Regional and National Adaptation Priorities in Central and West Africa (PACO)" is financed by the International Climate Initiative (IKI) through the German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) and implemented by GIZ in Benin, Republic of Congo, Côte d"Ivoire, and Senegal. The project is carried out by a consortium comprising the African Development Bank (AfDB), Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK), the Climate Commission of the Sahel Region (CCRS), and GIZ, in close collaboration with national ministries of environment, public and private actors, and civil society. PACO aims to strengthen climate resilience and adaptive capacities of governments, civil society, municipalities, and small and medium enterprises in the target countries. By supporting the implementation of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) and governance frameworks, the project seeks to protect livelihoods and enhance climate-resilient development in regions heavily dependent on the primary sector and therefore highly exposed to climate change impacts. To achieve this, PACO operates through four interlinked outputs: Regional Support and coordination: The Climate Commissions for the Sahel Region (CCRS) and the Congo Basin (CCBC) support and upscale climate resilience of their member states in line with international agendas. Climate Governance: The four target countries strengthen their national climate governance frameworks and adaptive capacities of key stakeholders. Sectoral approaches: Public and private investors implement transformative actions in priority sectors of the target countries' NAPs/NDCs to improve climate-resilient sectoral productivity. South-South collaboration: Key stakeholders engage in South-South collaboration and exchange experiences relevant to technology transfer. The present commission concentrates on activities under Outputs 3 and 4, with emphasis on the collaboration between GIZ and the two multilateral development banks-AfDB and IsDB. Under Output 3, the AfDB, through its Climate and Environment Finance Division, will select from five small-scale adaptation projects (20 in total), one per country (four in total) for demonstrating their Adaptation Benefits Mechanism (ABM). The ABM is a results-based financing approach developed by the AfDB to enhance the resilience of vulnerable communities and ecosystems. Officially recognized under the UNFCCC as the first non-market cooperative approach pursuant to Article 6.8 of the Paris Agreement, it provides a tool for mobilizing new adaptation finance and scaling successful measures across Africa. In parallel, the IsDB will update their pipeline of bankable climate adaptation projects in its member countries - Benin, Côte d"Ivoire, and Senegal - helping leverage public and private finance. Through cooperation with GIZ and other partners, the project targets mobilizing up to EUR 60 million in additional funds (including EUR 50 million from IsDB) for climate-resilient investments. Under Output 4, the IsDB, supported by GIZ, will implement a regional Reverse Linkage initiative to facilitate knowledge and technology transfer between countries. This includes establishing a Regional Centre of Excellence in West Africa to host reverse linkages, enabling member states to exchange expertise and best practices in adaptation and resilience. The Reverse Linkage mechanism, pioneered by IsDB, fosters technical cooperation among member countries to develop endogenous solutions. Through these coordinated efforts, the PACO project will contribute to scaling up climate adaptation action, improving institutional capacity, mobilizing finance, and fostering regional and international cooperation to enhance resilience in West and Central Africa.

description-proc.eng: The HUS Group requests tenders to procure test kit(s) for plasma and urine amino acids by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) based technology. The test kit(s) should contain all needed assay dependent products like reagents, calibrators, the manufacturer’s control samples, the method parameters for the LC-MS/MS instrumentation, product support and all other products needed for the assay except ordinary laboratory necessity, e.g. laboratory water, pipettes or glassware. Hotfix 4 or SCIEX OS software versions. In addition, basic laboratory instrumentation like mixers, incubators, pipetting robots and centrifuges are available. The kits are intended for the detection and quantitative analysis of amino acids in plasma and urine. The amino acid profile allows diagnosis and monitoring of inborn errors of metabolism. At present, HUS runs approximately 1000 plasma and 200 urine patient sample tests yearly. The runs are performed in approximately 2-3 batches a week and about 5-10 samples in one batch. Samples should be able to prepare in vials. The contract period is 48 months. ESTIMATED VALUE At present, HUS runs approximately 1000 plasma and 200 urine patient sample tests yearly. This is an estimate and the contracting entity does not commit to the stated consumption figures indicated in the invitation to tender. The final order quantities may be higher or lower than stated. No decision regarding the procurement procedure, supplier selection or award of a contract has been taken at this stage.
